stance.label: Taiwan bear deepens · stick to the plan

headline: Taiwan crashes 2,393 points, 3rd-biggest drop ever, −17.5% this week; 365 stocks limit-down
summary: Taiwan's bear market deepened today on panic and deleveraging: the new short-sale curbs did not stop the limit-down wave, and margin debt is down almost a quarter in a month. Foreign selling shrank for a second day; dealer hedging led the selling. Only 2 systemic lights are on, so it is not a downtrend yet. 0050 is 3.4% from its fifth tier; keep regular investing on plan.

overview.lead: Taiwan had a panic crash today: the US selloff, new chip export rules and thin liquidity on day one of short-sale curbs hit at once, wiping out almost a fifth in one week.
points: The TAIEX fell 2,393.6 points to 36,033.29, its third-biggest point drop ever.
It lost 17.5% this week and is −27.7% from the 10/6 high.
Turnover was NT$877.3B; 365 listed and OTC stocks hit limit-down.
Heavyweights fell across the board: TSMC (2330) fell 4.8% but held NT$2,000.
MediaTek (2454) and Delta (2308) hit limit-down; ASE (3711) fell 9.3%.
Korea's KOSPI fell 5.2% and the Nikkei almost 5%: AI stocks sold off across Asia.

focus.lead: The three Taiwan names took the hit, and 0050 is only 3.4% from its fifth tier; the Taiwan and Japan fund NAVs have not caught up with today's limit-down wave.
points: 0050 fell 6.4% and is −27.5% from its high.
0050's fifth tier is 81.55, 3.4% away.
SPY's second tier is still the closest of the nine, 2.1% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV only runs to 11/19, −38.4% from high; today's limit-down wave is not in it yet.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8): its top two, TSMC and MediaTek, fell hard today, so the next NAV will drop again.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV only runs to 11/18; two days of Taiwan losses and Japan's drop are not in it yet.
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend share 6 top-ten names, about 27% weight; they move together.

position.lead: None of the nine reached a new tier today; 0050 is closing in on its fifth tier, and its first four tiers have used 70% of the reserve under the framework.
points: 0050 fifth tier 81.55, 3.4% away.
SPY second tier 701.18, 2.1% away.
QQQ fourth tier 607.73, 5.8% away.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) fifth tier is 5.5% away (11/19 NAV).
AB American Growth (LU0683600562) second tier is 2.2% away (11/19 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used every tier; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: Today's new negative is chip controls, not the economy: US jobs and credit are still steady, and a December hike is still what weighs on stocks.
points: New US BIS chip export rules took effect on 11/19; Reuters says TSMC told Chinese clients to pause orders at 16nm and below.
TSMC declined to comment on market talk and said it will follow applicable laws and rules.
High-yield spread 3.47% (11/18), still far from the 5% warning line.
10-year Treasury yield 5.04%; NT dollar at 32.93 (11/19).
US PCE inflation on 11/25 is key for the size of a December hike.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan's fear has reached washout level: 4 of 5 bottoming signals are on; only extreme foreign selling is missing.
points: TAIEX RSI 26, oversold.
Margin debt is down 24.1% in a month and fell another NT$23.7B on 11/19.
Only 9% of stocks are above the 200-day line and 4% above the 50-day line.
531 new lows and 0 new highs.
CNN Fear & Greed 18.6, extreme fear.

sectors.lead: There was nowhere to hide today: every sector fell, and electronic components, the biggest winners of the last run, fell most.
points: Electronic components fell 9.5% and are down 43.5% in a month.
Plastics fell 9.1% and optoelectronics 8.2%.
Even the most resilient, IT services and household goods, fell 3% to 4%.
Market leader Aspeed (5274) and 23 stocks priced over NT$1,000 hit limit-down; high-priced names deleveraged hardest.
Domestic funds sold UMC (2303), CTBC (2891) and Cathay Financial (2882), and bought defensives such as Mega (2886) and Chunghwa Telecom (2412).

taiwan.lead: Foreign cash selling shrank for a second day; today's selling was led by dealer hedging and margin calls.
points: The three institutional groups sold a net NT$52.2B; foreigners sold for a fifth day.
Foreigners sold NT$9.4B today, far less than NT$76.6B on 11/18.
Dealers sold NT$34.1B, NT$29.0B of it from hedging books.
Foreigners have sold about NT$1.09T in a month.
Foreign net short in TAIEX futures is 97,863 contracts, down about 3,000 in five days.
TSMC ADR (TSM) premium 10.4% (11/19).

watch.lead: Tonight, watch whether US stocks end a six-day slide and how TSMC's ADR takes the export news; next week, whether Taiwan's limit-down count falls.
points: Tonight is US monthly options expiry, which can add volatility.
Tonight is TSMC ADR's first session since the export-control report.
The TAIEX must get back above 39,858 to leave the bear definition.
The S&P 500 has closed below its 200-day line 3 days in a row; two more makes 5.
US PCE on 11/25; US markets closed for Thanksgiving on 11/26.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is a bear with rising risk, not a downtrend: 2 systemic lights are on and the 200-day line is still rising.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 13.2% below its 200-day line, which is still up 3.2%.
Systemic lights: 2 on for Taiwan (US below its 200-day line, breadth collapse); credit, the economy and financial conditions are fine.
Credit is the safest area: the US high-yield spread is 3.47%, far from 5%.
Bottoming signals: 4 of 5 on (oversold, margin deleveraging, breadth washout, surge in new lows); only extreme foreign selling is missing.
History: all 6 episodes since 2000 that fell this far went past −20%, and 4 went past −30%.
The 12-month median for those 6 was +18.2%.
Only 1 fell as fast as this one; too few samples, reference only.
What would change the call: a close back above 39,858, then a week above the 200-day line at 41,527 → back to a pullback.
3+ systemic lights, or a flat 200-day line → a downtrend.
US stocks are still a pullback in an uptrend: only 1 systemic light is on for the S&P 500.
